- Top of page starts with discussion text
- Then "Cross-strategy deployment constraint." paragraph (this is from Limitations!)


- Then more Limitations paragraphs
- The page ends with "Ethics Statement"

So the Discussion overflows by just a few lines before Limitations kicks in, followed by the Ethics Statement at the bottom. I need to trim about 4 more lines from the Discussion to keep it compact.

Looking at the cross-strategy section, I can tighten the language significantly. Instead of spelling out all the details about mean accuracy, d0 recall, and d2 recall separately, I can combine the key findings into a more concise statement that still captures the main point: strategy-induced shifts are harder than architectural differences, and the real accuracy drop happens when you exclude the easy d0 cases, with d2 being the main problem area.

input.old_string:
Mean cross-strategy accuracy (59.1\%) falls 7pp below cross-model transfer (66.4\%), indicating that strategy-induced shifts pose a greater challenge than architectural differences.
As with cross-model transfer, d0 recall remains high ($\geq$89.5\%), inflating headline accuracy; excluding d0, d1--d3 accuracy drops further (45.9\%; chance = 33\%).
d2 recall ranges from 3.7\% to 19\%, confirming mid-chain depths as the primary confusion locus.
